title: Declare runtime contract and safety checklist for ad-hoc open-model ingest
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: This ticket defines a concise runtime contract and a safety checklist for ingesting ad-hoc / community open-model weights into the Redwood catalog. The goal is to reduce ambiguity during intake, make pinning decisions reproducible, and ensure the runtime team has the signals it needs to classify compatibility and select fallbacks. This PRD-level clarification narrows scope from a full onboarding overhaul to: 1) a minimal metadata schema that every open-model entry must provide, 2) deterministic runtime sanity tests we will run as part of CI, and 3) a decision playbook for soft vs hard pinning and rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: A 12-field intake metadata schema (JSON) exists and is documented in the catalog PRD; fields include model_id, declared_architecture, tokenizer_family, max_context_tokens, quantization_profiles, recommended_variants, license_url, provenance_notes, expected_kv_cache_behavior, sample_prompt_suite_url, backward_compatibility_notes, and suggested_fallback_aliases.

Automated sanity suite (unit smoke tests) runs on new ingest: - loads model, tokenizes canonical prompts, runs 3 representative generation traces, measures KV cache warm/cold paths, verifies no crash on extreme sequence lengths up to declared max_context_tokens.

A clear pinning rubric is defined: - Hard pin required if model fails deterministic runtime tests or introduces incompat kernel patterns; - Soft pin allowed if minor performance variance but passing sanity suite; - Soft-pin entries must include 'compatibility_notes' with explicit runtime caveats and a suggested fallback.

Rollback and degradation policy is documented: quantifiable thresholds for latency regression (>=30% p95 increase), token-quality regressions detected by eval harness (>=5% drop on critical evals), and error-rate spikes (>=3x baseline) that trigger immediate rollback to nearest pinned variant.
Catalog intake UI has 3 new required fields surfaced to the uploader and captured in the model record: 'declared_architecture', 'expected_kv_cache_behavior', and 'compatibility_notes'.

Console and runtime teams receive a machine-readable compatibility annotation (tag set) that can be used by routing and fallback policies (example tags: kv-cache:compatible, kv-cache:best-effort, quantized:8-bit-support, tokenizer:mismatch-risk).
Security review signoff present when 'security_review_required' flag is true; the intake flow blocks publication until security review status is attached.
Integration tests covered in a GH PR that exercises the intake flow end-to-end: submission -> automated tests -> tag emission -> runtime canary rollout to staging.

Documentation: PRD appendix provides 2 example filled intake records (one for an LLaMA-style family, one for a decoder-only transformer optimized for long context) and a template for compatibility_notes.
All acceptance criteria have associated owners and one-line runbook entries in the playbook for on-call and runtime to act on regressions.
decisions: Require declared max_context_tokens to be used as an upper bound in runtime scheduling and kernel-selection heuristics.
Adopt a soft-pin semantic: soft-pin allows runtime kernel adaptation and heuristic routing but does not become default for production traffic until further evaluation.
When automated tests detect KV-cache incompatibility, classify model as 'kv-cache:best-effort' and add a recommended fallback alias; schedule a follow-up deeper probe by runtime team.
Compatibility notes should be authored by the intake owner and signed off by a runtime SME before publication.
risks: R1: Model authors under-report tokenizer differences leading to silent degeneration in user prompts; mitigation: require sample_prompt_suite and tokenization diffs as part of CI.
R2: Overly conservative hard-pinning could block valuable models; mitigation: allow appeal path and 14-day probation soft-pin window backed by telemetry.
R3: Automation false positives blocking publish; mitigation: provide override with documented human review path and clear error categories.
